entities.summary:
P'arsman VI, of the Chosroid Dynasty, became the king (mepe) of Iberia in 561. The length of his reign is unknown. The royal power was largely nominal at that time as the Sassanid Empire dominated Iberia.

As the ruler of Iberia, P'arsman VI was part of the broader Chosroid Dynasty, which ruled over the region from 287 to 580 CE. His reign was marked by the continued influence of the Sassanid Empire, which had conquered Iberia in the 3rd century CE.

Despite the nominal power, P'arsman VI's reign had significant cultural and economic implications for the region. The Chosroid Dynasty played a key role in the spread of Christianity in Iberia, with P'arsman VI himself being baptized into the faith.

The legacy of P'arsman VI can be seen in the many churches and monasteries he built throughout Iberia, which became centers of learning and culture. The Chosroid Dynasty's influence also extended to the fields of art and architecture, with many of their buildings and artifacts still standing today.

In the 10th century, the Chosroid Dynasty was eventually replaced by the Bagratuni dynasty, which ruled over Iberia until the 11th century CE. P'arsman VI's reign may have been short, but its impact on the history of Iberia was significant.

P'arsman VI's story is also one of personal tragedy. The exact date of his death is unknown, but it is believed to have occurred in 599 CE. Despite this, his legacy lived on, and he remains an important figure in the history of Iberia.

P'arsman VI's reign was marked by the continued struggle for power between the Chosroid Dynasty and the Sassanid Empire. The Sassanid Empire, which ruled over much of the Middle East and Central Asia, had a profound impact on the region, bringing with it its own culture, language, and religion.
